messages:
sara_cs: Heads-up — got an enterprise customer who says removed users from an Okta group are still present in Redwood > they lose product access but show up in the org user list and role still attached. They call it a "ghost membership". Raised ticket 72314. need quick triage. :thinking_face:
liam_se: can you paste the SCIM logs from the org? sounds like group->role mapping not being applied on deprovision step. most common culprit is a partial group push or token scope that can't read groups.
sara_cs: pasted below (redacted):
```
[2026-03-12T09:14:02Z] SCIM: GET /v2/Groups?filter=displayName eq "rwd-engineers" -> 200 OK
[2026-03-12T09:14:03Z] SCIM: PATCH /v2/Groups/<group-id> (members removed) -> 204 No Content
[2026-03-12T09:14:05Z] Redwood: APPLY_ROLE_MAPPING group:<group-id> -> db queued
[2026-03-12T09:14:05Z] Provisioner: FETCH_GROUP_MEMBERS group:<group-id> -> 403 Forbidden (scim:Groups.read missing)
[2026-03-12T09:14:06Z] Deprovision: SKIP user:<user-id> -> still in users table, role not removed
```
liam_se: ok that 403 during FETCH_GROUP_MEMBERS is the smoking gun. Okta sometimes uses a token with only user scope if admin generated via API token UI. we expect the SCIM service account to have both Groups.read and Users.read (redwood expects `scim:Groups.read scim:Users.read scim:Users.write` depending on connector).
nate_prodops: adding repro steps I used locally to mirror:
1) create test org
2) create role mapping: okta group rwd-eng -> Redwood role 'engineer'
3) add user alice to rwd-eng in Okta and push -> user appears with role 'engineer' in Redwood (good)
4) remove alice from rwd-eng via Okta UI and push -> Okta push returns 204, but our worker logs 403 when fetching group members -> alice still has 'engineer' role in DB
Command I used to simulate group fetch using the customer's token:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <SCIM_TOKEN_REDACTED>" "https://customerscim.okta.com/scim/v2/Groups/<group-id>/members"
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{
  "errorCode": "E0000007",
  "errorSummary": "Insufficient authentication",
}
```
sara_cs: customer says they rotated the connector token two weeks ago. could that have changed scopes?
liam_se: If they replaced a token with an API token generated from Okta admin -> that token commonly lacks SCIM group scopes. Only tokens created via SCIM Service App (or with explicit scopes) will include group read/write. We should ask customer to confirm how token was created (SCIM integration vs generic API token).
eva_infra: quick note on our side — our system currently treats any non-200 from group fetch as a hard skip for that deprovisioning cycle to avoid accidental mass removals. We log an alert but don't auto-remove roles without a successful group membership confirmation. That behavior prevents dangerous deletes but causes these "ghost" entries until next successful sync. We could change to retry/backoff sooner, but still need correct scopes.
liam_se: proposed immediate mitigation steps for the customer (fastest path):
- Verify SCIM integration app in Okta (not generic token). If using generic API token, create a SCIM Service App and generate credentials.
- In Okta, enable Group Push or ensure Group Push includes full membership sync.
- Re-run a full sync from our console: Settings -> SCIM -> Force full sync (this will re-fetch group membership once token fixed).
- Optional: temporarily mark role mapping to 'deprovision directly' (dangerous) only if customer accepts potential risk.
sara_cs: I told them to check token creation method. customer asked for exact scopes we need to ask their Okta admin for — what wording to give them?
liam_se: tell them: "We require a SCIM credential with group read capability. In Okta, use the 'Provisioning' -> 'Configure API Integration' flow and enable 'Enable API Integration' on the SCIM app; ensure group push (or group read) is enabled. The token must be created by the SCIM app so it includes group access. If using a custom connector, grant scopes: scim.Groups.read scim.Groups.write scim.Users.read scim.Users.write."
sara_cs: they pushed back — "Our security team won't create a new token without justification." Any audit-friendly explanation we can provide?
nate_prodops: paste for audit: "When the SCIM connector token lacks groups:read scope, Redwood cannot verify membership changes and will skip deprovision to avoid accidental data loss. This leads to users remaining assigned to roles until a subsequent successful membership fetch. Requesting SCIM token with explicit group read/write scopes is necessary to ensure deterministic deprovisioning and compliance with their access removal SLA."
eva_infra: added follow-up tooling idea: we can add a health-check endpoint in the console that validates the token scopes by issuing a dry-run group query and surfacing which scopes are missing. low-effort and reduces back-and-forth. filing infra ticket INF-824.
sara_cs: customer fixed token creation method and gave us a new token. they asked for a step-by-step to confirm it's working without waiting for full sync window.
liam_se: steps to validate quickly:
1) use the customer's token and `curl GET /scim/v2/Groups/<group-id>` — expect 200 and `members` array present
2) remove a fixture user from Okta group and push a Group PATCH that removes the member -> Okta returns 204
3) call our internal job endpoint (or click Force full sync) and watch worker logs: you should see FETCH_GROUP_MEMBERS succeed and APPLY_ROLE_MAPPING remove role for the user
Example curl for (1):
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <SCIM_TOKEN>" "https://customerscim.okta.com/scim/v2/Groups/<group-id>" | jq '.members'
[ { "value": "00u1...", "display": "alice@example.com" } ]
```
sara_cs: ran those checks with the new token — GET returns members, and after forcing full sync the user role vanished as expected. customer is happy and asked for a short postmortem they can include in their ticket.
liam_se: postmortem note you can paste into ticket: "Root cause: SCIM connector token used by the Okta->Redwood integration was created without group read scope (likely a generic API token), causing our worker to receive 403 when attempting to fetch group members during deprovision. Redwood's safe-guard prevents automatic role removals on failed membership fetches, resulting in transient 'ghost' memberships. Remediation: rotated to a SCIM integration token created through Okta's Provisioning flow (with group read/write scopes) and forced a full sync, which resolved the stale role assignments. Recommended: enable console token health-check and add scoped token docs to onboarding flow."
sara_cs: pasted and closed ticket 72314. thanks y'all. :tada:
